findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot paginate datetime fields
findings.body: OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint uses OptimizedCursorPaginator with order_by="-datetime" (organization_auditlogs.py:79). This paginator's get_item_key assumes a numeric key and calls math.floor/math.ceil on the value, but the value is a datetime.datetime for audit logs. math.floor raises TypeError ("must be real number, not datetime") as soon as build_cursor processes the first non-empty page, so the optimized pagination path returns a 500. It should use the timestamp conversion logic from DateTimePaginator, both in get_item_key and value_from_cursor, or not be used with datetime fields.

findings.title: Negative cursor offsets hit unsupported Django negative slicing
findings.body: The advanced branch intentionally sets start_offset = cursor.offset when it is negative and then evaluates queryset[start_offset:stop]. Django QuerySet does not support negative indexing and raises ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported. The comment claiming the ORM handles negative slicing is false. A crafted cursor with a negative offset (for example via Cursor.from_string, which accepts negative offsets) will cause a 500 instead of the advertised reverse pagination. The non-advanced is_prev fallthrough can also pass a negative offset.

findings.title: Redis set-to-zset change breaks existing buffered segments and rolling deploys
findings.body: The span buffer storage is changed from Redis SETs (SADD/SUNIONSTORE/SCARD/SSCAN) to sorted sets (ZADD/ZUNIONSTORE/ZCARD/ZSCAN), but the same span-buf:s:* keys are reused. Keys already buffered by the old code, and keys written by old consumers during a rolling deploy, are still SET type. New code executing ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE/ZADD/ZSCAN on those keys, or old code executing S* commands on zsets, will get WRONGTYPE errors and affected segments will be lost or fail to flush. Use a versioned key namespace, a migration window, or otherwise prevent mixed-version access.

findings.title: Eviction can remove the segment/root span and silently drops spans
findings.body: The new cap calls zpopmin to remove the entries with the lowest end_timestamp_precise scores. Evicted spans are never flushed and there is no metric or log recording that data was dropped. If the segment/root span has the lowest score (possible with clock skew or particular is_segment spans), it can be evicted while has_root_span_key is still set, so the buffer later flushes a segment whose segment_id points to a missing root span and no span is marked is_segment. Eviction should preserve the segment span and at least account for/report evicted spans.

findings.title: No tests for OptimizedCursorPaginator or Lua eviction behavior
findings.body: The new OptimizedCursorPaginator is completely untested, and none of the changed span buffer tests exercises the new >1000 span zpopmin eviction branch in add-buffer.lua. This leaves the first-page datetime TypeError, negative-offset crash, and root-span eviction behavior uncaught, despite all being reachable in the newly added optimized endpoint path or normal buffer operation.
